segments.voice: Yesterday, the whole five years in seven sits began at the first doorway: Ganesha honored first, clear the road, then begin. Today, the second look back.

A favorite song sounds different the first time it's heard on good headphones: a bass line, a second voice, a whole layer that was always there underneath. Year two of this path was that layer. After a year of first words and stories, it opened the texts underneath them: the big Upanishads, Patanjali's Yoga Sutras, the Ramayana read part by part, and a year of festivals.
screen: `A LAYER UNDERNEATH.` → `YEAR TWO: THE TEXTS THEMSELVES.`

segments.voice: Here's the second sit, lightly. In the Chandogya, a father hands his son salt and water, and the son can't find the salt, though every sip tastes of it. Tat tvam asi: you are that. In the Brihadaranyaka, Maitreyi asks what wealth would be worth if it couldn't make her free of death. Patanjali defines yoga in one short line, the stilling of the mind's turnings, before he says a word about posture. And Valmiki's Ramayana, read as a serial, turned a story people already knew into a text people could read for themselves. That was year two's gift: not new stories, but the ground under the old ones. And this year's great sayings grew from those same roots. Tat tvam asi came back as one of four. The honey teaching came back to close ayam atma brahma. The texts read in year two became the texts chanted around in these last weeks. Now this week, in one breath. Full from full. Ears first. Strength, and no turning away. Speech rooted in mind. A golden lid. I will, then I have. And a doorway, honored first.
screen: `SALT IN WATER: YOU ARE THAT.` · `YOGA: THE MIND'S TURNINGS, STILLED.` · `THE RAMAYANA, READ FOR ITSELF.` · `THE ROOTS OF THE GREAT SAYINGS.`
